title: LLMutantKiller: Using Large Language Models to Generate Tests that Kill Mutants
read_source: https://www.franktip.org/pubs/issta2026.pdf (coauthor-hosted 23-page full paper; ACM DOI 10.1145/3832098 verified via final author artifact and ISSTA listing)
datasets: StrykerJS-generated surviving mutants from 13 open-source JavaScript/TypeScript projects; population 1,956 surviving mutants, Cochran sample selected 915. Manual classification found 815 behavior-changing and 100 equivalent mutants. Sample spans projects such as Complex.js, q, delta, plural, node-dirty and others. No Defects4J/BugsInPy/SWT-Bench experiment.
task: Given a surviving StrykerJS mutant and original/mutated source, generate a Jest/TypeScript test that passes on original and fails on mutant; filter syntax/dependency/execution failures and iteratively re-prompt with scenario-specific feedback (up to 10 attempts). Manual audit distinguishes behaviorally valid tests from source-introspection cheating and equivalent mutants.
input_setting: Original JS/TS file with mutation site replaced by placeholder; mutation metadata with original and replacement code fragments; optional existing project tests and package.json context. Output is a single Jest test file. Tests may use existing allowed libraries but cannot inspect source text or use external dependencies not already allowed. This is mutant-directed test generation, not issue-report-to-BRT or historical real-bug analysis.
author_artifact_url: https://github.com/neu-se/LLMutantKiller___Artifact (official source, Docker and full replication package); author-hosted paper PDF https://www.franktip.org/pubs/issta2026.pdf.
author_relationship_evidence: Paper is listed by coauthor Frank Tip at the official publications page; ISSTA 2026 page and author-linked GitHub repository identify final article DOI 10.1145/3832098 and ISSTA007. Repository calls itself the paper companion/replication package and includes implementation, prompts, mutation metadata, full stored experiment outputs, manual labels and TestPilot results. Current main commit API SHA `ec7b46370e63035ae3229bf7a89e3737c005ab9a` (mutable main). Artifact LICENSE separates author-owned MIT software from CC BY 4.0 docs and preserves third-party project licenses.
source_commit_or_archive: Author artifact GitHub `neu-se/LLMutantKiller___Artifact` main observed at `ec7b46370e63035ae3229bf7a89e3737c005ab9a`; implementation in source-code/ TypeScript, templates, mutation metadata and CLI; 553 MB tracked paper_results in truncated GitHub API tree and artifact docs estimate 1.7 GB compressed/9 GB extracted. Static-inspected README, LICENSE, CLAIMS, REPRODUCIBILITY, REPRODUCING, REQUIREMENTS and `source-code/src/core/ChatClient.ts`; no code executed. Custom `OPENROUTER_LLM_API_ENDPOINT` plus user-provided auth headers are supported, so OpenAI-compatible custom model endpoints are possible in principle.
license: Author-owned software and experiment artifacts MIT; author documentation CC BY 4.0. Third-party subject repository/code/data retain upstream licenses and must be checked individually. Paper itself ACM author-copyrighted; paper text accessible from coauthor site.
exact_models: All routed via OpenRouter API; temperature 0.5, 10 attempts, 300s timeout. The source supports a configurable OpenAI-compatible chat-completion endpoint, so own Qwen endpoint integration may be feasible but was not run.
weights_status: No checkpoint required in repository; experiment uses provider APIs. Devstral and Llama are open-weight model families, Claude is hosted. Model revisions are named by API/provider IDs; outputs are nondeterministic and provider updates may change. Own local Qwen can potentially use custom API endpoint/auth headers but differs from the tested models.
evaluation_route: Read all 15,171 extracted words / 1,614 lines of the 23-page author-hosted paper, including methods, full tables, threats, conclusions and references; PDF SHA-256 b63dd28ea79d3b7dd91dca008bd942535e255e77c5bd8d45f9b2ee2856a5ec13, text SHA-256 e43ee7976b4851e8cbb89bd0155c4e1a70bc322fa94eebb659270c54b8e95ba6. 915 random surviving mutants from 13 JS/TS projects; 815 classified behavior-changing and 100 equivalent. Claude Sonnet 4.6 without existing tests kills 811/915; after manual invalid-test filtering, valid tests kill 777/815 non-equivalent mutants (95.3%). With existing tests in prompt: 763/815 valid kills (93.6%); union of prompt variants kills 798/815 (97.9%). Devstral 2512: 509/815 (62.4%); Llama 3.3 70B: 216/815 (26.5%). TestPilot baseline kills 77/915. Up to 3.7% of mutants are killed only by invalid/source-introspection tests. Full source/artifact stores prompts, test outputs, logs, labels and analyses. Paper cost: ~$253 for one Claude config with caching, ~$1,313 approximate for 12 full configs; native time 456.6h and Docker extrapolation ~2,587h/108 days; 13-mutant/one-attempt demo <$1, 17 min Docker. No model/API/source execution.
blockers: Full live reproduction is resource- and API-intensive: artifact estimates ~456.6 native hours or ~108 Docker days for all 12 runs, about $1,313 at historical rates; full compressed artifact ~1.7 GB, extracted ~9 GB, 20 GB free disk, Linux amd64 Docker, 13 Node repositories.

The 13-mutant reduced live run is feasible (~17 minutes in Docker, <$1 at historical Devstral prices) and a CLI smoke test takes ~5 seconds; stored paper outputs can be inspected without API credentials.
Live results are nondeterministic; model provider routing/revisions, rate limits and caching may differ from paper. Exact byte-identical replication is not expected.
Paper studies JS/TS surviving Stryker mutants, not real Defects4J/BugsInPy/SWT issue bugs. It supplies mutation fragments rather than root-cause diagnosis or issue text.
Manual test-validity and mutant-equivalence decisions require human judgment and cannot be fully regenerated automatically. TestPilot execution infrastructure is upstream and not bundled.
Author source is MIT, but third-party subject code/data remain under their own licenses. No test/model code was run or source modified.
concept_fit: Very high for behavioral-difference-driven, bug-revealing test generation and oracle validity: tests must pass the original, fail the specific changed behavior, and avoid introspection or implementation cheating; execution feedback is categorized (syntax, dependencies, fail on original, pass on mutant). It can support a concept/expected-vs-actual test-generation comparison and expose false-positive test construction. It is not issue-level root-cause diagnosis, a real-bug benchmark, or Defects4J/SWT-Bench study.
recommendation: Promote as the strongest fully source-backed mutant-directed test-generation baseline among the recent papers reviewed. Public MIT implementation, complete prompts, mutation metadata, Docker, manual labels and stored outputs make artifact inspection highly reproducible. An own Qwen model could likely be evaluated through the configurable OpenAI-compatible endpoint, but this has not been tested and remains distinct from reproducing the paper’s three model backbones. Start with stored-result analysis or documented 13-mutant smoke route; full original rerun is expensive. Pair with #52 for Defects4J real-fault oracle evidence and #55 for repository issue-reproducer quality; LLMutantKiller itself uses only generated mutants.
